title: Free Online Document Tools — No Signup, Private
heading: Everyday tools. Entirely in your browser.
description: Free document and image tools that run in your browser — scan, edit and compress PDFs, extract text, redact scans and remove backgrounds. No signup.
intro: Choose a tool, finish your task, and download the result. Your files are processed on your device, with no account required.
steps: Choose a document or image tool.
Add files from your device and adjust the result.
Download your files without a watermark.

faqs.q: Are these tools free without signup?
faqs.a: Yes. Scanner.cam tools require no account and add no watermarks. Device memory and browser storage limit how many files you can process.

faqs.q: Are my files uploaded?
faqs.a: No. File processing runs in your browser. Some tools download processing models or recognition files on first use.

faqs.q: Can I use these tools on my phone?
faqs.a: You can use the tools in a supported mobile browser. Camera access, file decoding, performance, and available memory depend on your device and browser.

faqs.q: Do the tools work offline?
faqs.a: Some processing files must be downloaded on first use. Availability offline depends on which assets your browser has cached; keep an internet connection available when trying a feature for the first time.

faqs.q: Which tools does Scanner.cam offer?
faqs.a: A document scanner, a background remover, a PDF page editor, a PDF compressor, image-to-text OCR, a PDF redaction tool and a book-page flattener — all free, all in your browser.

faqs.q: Do I need an app for these tools?
faqs.a: No. Every tool opens in a browser on phones, tablets and computers. Nothing to install and no account to create.

faqs.q: Can I use these tools for work documents?
faqs.a: Yes. Files are processed on your device and never uploaded, which suits sensitive documents — but always review outputs before sharing, especially redacted files.

faqs.q: What is the difference between the PDF editor and compress PDF?
faqs.a: The PDF editor changes pages — their order, rotation, or which pages are kept — and combines PDFs and photos into one file. Compress PDF changes file size toward a target like 1 MB. Use the editor first, then compress.

answer: Scanner.cam provides free browser-based document and image tools. Choose a tool, add a file, and download the result without an account. Processing happens on your device. Scanner.cam offers free document and image tools that run entirely in your browser: scan documents with your camera, remove photo backgrounds, edit and combine PDF pages, compress scanned PDFs to a target size, extract text with OCR, redact sensitive details, and flatten curved book pages. No signup, no app install, no file uploads — processing happens on your device and results download straight to it.

sections.heading: Choose a tool for your task
paragraphs: Use the document scanner to photograph paper and make a PDF. Use the PDF page editor to combine pages, or the compressor when a submission has a file-size limit.
For images, remove a background and download a transparent PNG. OCR extracts text, redaction covers sensitive parts of scans, and manual curve correction helps straighten gently bowed pages.

sections.heading: Privacy and availability
paragraphs: Your document and image contents are processed locally in your browser. Some features need an internet connection on first use to download recognition or processing files.
Files and saved sessions are subject to browser storage and device memory. On a shared device, download your results and clear saved scans when finished.

title: Remove Background Online Free — Transparent PNG
heading: Free Background Remover Online
description: Remove a photo background free in your browser — no signup, no upload, no watermark. Preview the cutout and download a transparent PNG.
intro: Turn portraits and product photos into transparent PNGs. Choose a photo, remove the background, and download the result. Your image stays on your device.
steps: Choose a JPG, PNG, WebP, or HEIC photo, or drop it into the upload area.
Select Remove background. Processing files download on first use.
Compare the original with the cutout and download your transparent PNG.

faqs.q: How can I remove a background for free?
faqs.a: Choose a photo in Scanner.cam, select Remove background, then download the transparent PNG. No account, subscription, or watermark is required.

faqs.q: Does my photo leave my device?
faqs.a: No. Background removal runs locally in your browser. The first use needs internet to download processing files.

faqs.q: Which photos work best?
faqs.a: Portraits and product photos with a clear subject work best. Hair, glass, fine edges, and busy scenes may need further editing. Always review the cutout.

faqs.q: Is this a free remove.bg alternative?
faqs.a: Scanner.cam offers browser-based background removal and transparent PNG downloads without signup. Results depend on the photo and may differ from other services.

faqs.q: What file will I download?
faqs.a: The result is a PNG with transparency. PNG preserves the transparent background when you place the image over another design.

faqs.q: Why are the edges of my cutout imperfect?
faqs.a: The automatic model estimates the subject boundary. Fine hair, glass, similar colors, and cluttered backgrounds can make that boundary harder to identify. Try a clearer photo and review the result.

faqs.q: Can I remove the background from a product photo for an online listing?
faqs.a: Yes. Upload the product photo, remove the background and download the transparent PNG, then place it on a white background in any editor if a marketplace requires one.

faqs.q: Does the background remover work on my phone?
faqs.a: Yes. It runs in your phone’s browser. The small on-device model downloads once and is then cached, so later removals start faster.

faqs.q: What is a transparent PNG?
faqs.a: A PNG image whose background pixels carry no colour, so the subject can sit on any colour, photo or slide. JPG cannot do this — it always fills the background with a solid colour.

faqs.q: Can it cut out hair or fur cleanly?
faqs.a: It works best where the subject stands out clearly from the background. Fine hair edges are approximate, so always preview the cutout before downloading.

answer: Upload a JPG, PNG, WebP, or HEIC photo, choose Remove background, then download the transparent PNG. The image is processed in your browser without an account or photo upload. Scanner.cam's background remover runs a small AI model entirely on your device: upload a JPG, PNG, WebP or HEIC photo, the background is removed in your browser, and you download a transparent PNG. No account, no upload, no watermark. It works best on photos with a clear subject; hair and busy backgrounds may leave faint edges, so preview before downloading.

sections.heading: When to use a transparent background
paragraphs: A transparent PNG can be placed over a different color, design, or slide. It is useful for product photos, profile pictures, presentation graphics, and simple cutouts.
Choose a photo with a clear subject and separation from its background. A sharp image with even lighting usually gives the remover a better starting point.

sections.heading: Review the cutout before using it
paragraphs: Automatic removal can soften hair, transparent objects, shadows, or other fine details. Compare the result with the original and check the edges before using the PNG.
Photos are limited to 40 MB and 20 megapixels. The processing files download on first use; the photo itself is not uploaded.

title: Reorder PDF Pages Online Free — Merge, Rotate, Delete
heading: Edit and Combine PDF Pages Online
description: Reorder, rotate or delete PDF pages free in your browser — no signup, no upload. Combine PDFs and photos into one PDF and export it. Pages become images.
intro: Combine existing PDFs with document photos in one workspace. Reorder, rotate, or remove pages before exporting a new PDF. Imported pages become images; original links, forms, signatures, and text layers are not preserved.
steps: Upload PDFs or images from your device.
Use the Pages panel to reorder or remove pages, and Rotate to turn the selected page.
Choose Export to download your combined PDF.

faqs.q: Can I combine a PDF with scanned photos?
faqs.a: Yes. Upload PDFs and photos into the same workspace, arrange the pages, and export one document. Processing stays on your device.

faqs.q: Can I edit PDF text or preserve digital signatures?
faqs.a: No. This is a page editor. PDF pages are rendered as images, so links, forms, digital signatures, and existing text layers are not retained. Keep your original file.

faqs.q: Can I import password-protected PDFs?
faqs.a: Password-protected files are not supported. Unlock a copy using a trusted tool before importing it.

faqs.q: How do I reorder PDF pages?
faqs.a: After importing the PDF, use the up and down controls in the Pages panel or drag pages into the order you want, then export a new PDF.

faqs.q: Will the original PDF be changed?
faqs.a: No. Importing creates a working copy in your browser, and exporting downloads a new PDF. Keep the original file if you need its existing text, links, forms, or signatures.

faqs.q: Can I merge two PDFs into one PDF?
faqs.a: Yes. Import both PDFs, and photos too if needed, arrange the pages and export a single combined PDF.

faqs.q: Can I delete pages from a PDF online?
faqs.a: Yes. Remove any pages in the Pages panel before export. Your original file is never changed.

faqs.q: Can I rotate a sideways scanned page?
faqs.a: Yes. Select the page, rotate it the right way up, then export.

faqs.q: Does reordering PDF pages change the page content?
faqs.a: No. Only the order changes. Note that the export is image-based: the original text layer, links, forms and signatures are not preserved.

answer: Upload PDFs or document photos, arrange the pages, and export a combined PDF. The page editor runs locally; imported PDF pages are rendered as images. Scanner.cam's PDF page editor runs entirely in your browser: import PDFs and photos, drag or move pages into order, rotate sideways scans, remove unwanted pages, and export one combined PDF — no signup and no file upload. Imported PDF pages are rendered as images, so links, forms, signatures and selectable text are not carried into the export, and password-protected PDFs are not supported. Imports are limited to 80 MB and 100 pages.

sections.heading: Combine and arrange pages
paragraphs: Add a PDF, photos, or both. Select a page to rotate or crop it, use the Pages panel to change the order, and remove any pages you do not need.
Export creates a new PDF from the pages shown in the workspace. Use Undo if you need to recover a page removed during the current session.

sections.heading: Understand what the export preserves
paragraphs: Imported PDF pages become images. Existing selectable text, links, forms, and digital signatures are not carried into the new file; keep the original when those features matter.
A single PDF import is limited to 80 MB and 100 pages. Device memory and browser storage also affect large jobs; split large documents into smaller batches.

title: Compress PDF to 1MB Online Free — Scanned PDFs
heading: Compress a Scanned PDF to Your Size Limit
description: Compress a scanned PDF toward 1 MB, 500 KB or a custom size, free in your browser. See the measured output size before download — no signup, no upload.
intro: Upload a scanned PDF or photos, then choose a size limit in Export. Compression adjusts image resolution and quality locally. Very small limits may be impossible without losing readability; the tool tells you when the limit cannot be met.
steps: Upload your scanned PDF or document photos.
Open Export and choose 500 KB, 1 MB, or a custom limit.
Check the measured file size and quality preview before downloading.

faqs.q: Can I make a PDF smaller than 1 MB?
faqs.a: Choose a 1 MB target in Export. Scanner.cam tries progressively smaller image settings and measures the actual PDF. If the limit cannot be met, it shows an error instead of silently downloading an oversized file.

faqs.q: Will compression preserve editable PDF text?
faqs.a: Imported PDFs are converted to page images. Existing text layers, links, forms, and digital signatures are not retained. Keep the original PDF and check readability before submitting the compressed copy.

faqs.q: Can I set a custom PDF size limit?
faqs.a: Yes. Open Export, choose Custom limit, and enter a value in KB. The tool uses 1 KB = 1,000 bytes for the target and checks the actual output.

faqs.q: Why does my compressed PDF look less sharp?
faqs.a: Smaller files can require lower resolution or stronger JPEG compression. Try a larger target or export fewer pages, then inspect all pages before submitting.

faqs.q: How do I compress a PDF to 500 KB?
faqs.a: Choose the 500 KB target. The tool tries image settings locally and shows the measured output size before you download, so you can see whether the target was reached.

faqs.q: Can I compress a PDF for email?
faqs.a: Yes. Pick a target that fits the attachment limit and check the measured size shown before downloading.

faqs.q: Why is my scanned PDF so large?
faqs.a: A scanned PDF stores every page as an image, so file size grows with page count and scan resolution. Compression re-encodes those page images at lower settings to shrink the file.

faqs.q: Do I need to upload my PDF to compress it?
faqs.a: No. Compression runs entirely in your browser; the file never leaves your device.

answer: Upload a scanned PDF or photos, open Export, and choose a maximum size. Scanner.cam tries image settings locally and shows the measured PDF size before download. Scanner.cam compresses scanned PDFs entirely in your browser: upload a scanned PDF or photos, pick a maximum size — 500 KB, 1 MB or a custom limit — and the tool tries image settings locally, then shows the measured output size before you download. No signup, no upload, no watermark. Very small targets can soften scanned text, so preview readability before downloading and keep your original.

sections.heading: Choose a practical size target
paragraphs: Select 500 KB, 1 MB, 2 MB, or enter a custom limit in kilobytes. The compressor tests progressively smaller image settings and checks the generated PDF against the chosen limit.
If it cannot reach the limit with the available settings, it reports the smallest result and asks you to use a larger limit or fewer pages. It does not silently download an oversized result.

sections.heading: Check readability and preserve your original
paragraphs: Reducing image resolution and JPEG quality can make small or faint text harder to read. Preview the first page and inspect every page of the downloaded PDF before submitting it.
Imported PDFs are converted to page images. Existing text layers, links, forms, and digital signatures are not retained. Keep the source PDF when you need those features.

title: Image to Text Converter Free — OCR JPG, PNG & PDF
heading: Extract Text from Images and Scanned PDFs
description: Convert images and scanned PDFs to text free in your browser. On-device OCR in English, Spanish, French, German, Hindi or Arabic — download text, no signup.
intro: Turn document photos and scanned PDF pages into editable text. Recognition runs on your device in six languages. First use downloads recognition files; review the output for errors.
steps: Upload document photos or a scanned PDF.
Choose Extract text, then select the recognition language.
Download recognized text as a Unicode .txt file. English, Spanish, French, and German can also be embedded in a searchable PDF.

faqs.q: Which OCR languages are supported?
faqs.a: English, Spanish, French, German, Hindi, and Arabic are available for text downloads. Searchable PDF export supports English, Spanish, French, and German. Hindi and Arabic are currently available as Unicode text downloads only.

faqs.q: Does OCR upload my documents?
faqs.a: No. Recognition runs locally in your browser. Recognition files download on first use; document images are not uploaded.

faqs.q: Can I copy text from a scanned photo?
faqs.a: Yes. Recognize the image in a supported language and download the text file. Review it against the original because OCR can misread characters.

faqs.q: Why is my OCR result inaccurate?
faqs.a: Blur, shadows, small type, handwriting, and the wrong language selection can reduce accuracy. Try a sharper, upright image with even light and select the matching language.

faqs.q: Can I convert a JPG to text?
faqs.a: Yes. Upload the JPG, select the language of the text and download the recognized text.

faqs.q: Can I extract text from a scanned PDF?
faqs.a: Yes. Scanned PDF pages are recognized on your device and the text can be downloaded as a UTF-8 text file.

faqs.q: Can OCR read a screenshot?
faqs.a: Yes, if the text in the screenshot is clear and high-resolution. Small or blurry screenshot text gives worse results.

faqs.q: Does OCR work on handwritten notes?
faqs.a: The tool is built for printed text. Handwriting may be recognized, but results vary — treat handwritten output as a draft and check it against the original.

answer: Upload a document photo or scanned PDF, open Extract text, select a language, and download the recognized text as a UTF-8 text file. Recognition runs locally after the language files download. Scanner.cam's image-to-text tool runs OCR entirely in your browser: upload a document photo or scanned PDF, pick the language — English, Spanish, French, German, Hindi or Arabic — and download the recognized text as a UTF-8 file. No signup and no document upload; the language files download once and recognition runs on your device. Clear printed text works best; check names, numbers and punctuation against the original.

sections.heading: Turn a scan into text
paragraphs: Use a sharp, evenly lit scan with the page upright. Add one or more images or PDF pages, then select Extract text and choose the language that matches the document.
Download the recognized text as a .txt file and review names, numbers, punctuation, and layout. OCR is an estimate and accuracy depends on the scan.

sections.heading: Searchable PDF and language support
paragraphs: English, Spanish, French, German, Hindi, and Arabic are supported for text downloads. Searchable PDFs are available in English, Spanish, French, and German.
Hindi and Arabic are currently available as text downloads, not searchable PDF layers. Word positions in a searchable PDF may be imperfect, so check the exported document.

title: Redact PDF Online Free — Black Out Text Permanently
heading: Redact Sensitive Information from Scans
description: Redact a PDF free in your browser — cover sensitive details with boxes that replace the pixels, so hidden text cannot be recovered. No signup, no upload.
intro: Hide private details in document photos and scanned PDFs. Applied boxes replace the covered pixels in exported files. Original files and local undo history remain on your device until you clear them.
steps: Upload a scanned PDF or photo and select a page.
Choose Redact, draw boxes or enter their coordinates, and apply redactions.
Review every page, then export. Clear saved scans when finished on a shared device.

faqs.q: Can someone remove the black boxes from the exported PDF?
faqs.a: Applied redactions replace image pixels before PDF generation. The exported file contains the covered page image, rather than a removable overlay. Review the output and ensure every sensitive area is covered.

faqs.q: Does this delete my original document?
faqs.a: No. Your original file and local undo history are retained on your device. Clear saved scans after exporting when working on a shared device.

faqs.q: Should I redact every page separately?
faqs.a: Yes. Select and inspect each page, apply boxes wherever sensitive information appears, and verify the entire exported file.

faqs.q: Can I undo a redaction?
faqs.a: Yes, the current session supports Undo. Undo restores an earlier version, so check the final page and exported file before sharing it.

faqs.q: Can I black out text in a scanned PDF?
faqs.a: Yes. Scanned pages are images, so you draw boxes over the areas to hide and the pixels are replaced before export.

faqs.q: Is blacking out text with a black box permanent?
faqs.a: Here, yes. The boxes replace the underlying pixels in the exported image-based file, so the covered content is not in the exported file at all — unlike a highlight drawn over a text layer, which can be removed. Always review the exported file before sharing.

faqs.q: Can I redact a photo of a document?
faqs.a: Yes. Document photos work the same way as scanned PDFs.

faqs.q: Can I redact a signature or photo inside a PDF?
faqs.a: Yes. Boxes cover any area, not just text — signatures, photos, stamps and logos included.

answer: Upload a scanned PDF or photo, select a page, and apply redaction boxes over sensitive areas. The boxes replace image pixels before the new PDF or image is exported. Scanner.cam's redaction tool runs entirely in your browser: upload a scanned PDF or document photo, draw boxes over names, numbers, signatures or any sensitive area, and export a new PDF or image. The boxes replace the underlying pixels before export, so the covered content is not recoverable from the exported file — unlike a highlight drawn over a text layer. No signup, no upload. Always review the exported file before sharing, and keep your original.

sections.heading: How to redact a scanned document
paragraphs: Select each page that contains sensitive information. Choose Redact, draw boxes over the information or enter box coordinates, and apply them. Repeat for every page that needs redaction.
Review the page after applying boxes, then review the exported PDF or image. Make boxes large enough to cover the complete text, including edges and nearby copies.

sections.heading: Protect the original and saved session
paragraphs: Redaction changes the working image used for export. The original file is not deleted, and undo history can retain an earlier version in the current session.
On a shared device, export the redacted copy and clear saved scans when finished. Close any other tabs containing the original; they can retain their own local view.

title: Flatten Book Scans Free — Straighten Curved Pages
heading: Straighten Gentle Curves in Book Scans
description: Flatten curved book and notebook scans free in your browser. Manual top and bottom bend controls, live preview, no signup, no upload — gentle curves only.
intro: Use manual curve controls to straighten gently bowed lines in book and notebook photos. Preview the result before applying. Complex page folds or strong curves may still need a new photo.
steps: Upload a document photo and select the page.
Choose Flatten curved page and adjust the top and bottom bends.
Review the preview, apply the correction, and export. Undo is available if you want to try again.

faqs.q: Is curved-page correction automatic?
faqs.a: No. You adjust the top and bottom bends manually and review the preview. This correction works best for gentle curves; it cannot recover text hidden by folds or deep shadows.

faqs.q: Does this work like perspective cropping?
faqs.a: Perspective cropping adjusts the four document corners. Curve correction changes how the image is sampled between its top and bottom boundaries to reduce gentle vertical bowing.

faqs.q: Can I preview or undo a correction?
faqs.a: Yes. The controls show a preview before you apply the change, and Undo can restore the earlier page during the current session.

faqs.q: Why does my book page still look distorted?
faqs.a: The manual controls work best for gentle vertical curves. A deep fold, a page hidden by the binding, or a strongly angled photo may need a new image or a different correction workflow.

faqs.q: How do I flatten a book page photo?
faqs.a: Upload the page photo, choose the flatten control, adjust the top and bottom bend controls, preview the correction, then apply and export.

faqs.q: Can I flatten a photo of a notebook page?
faqs.a: Yes. Notebook pages work the same way as book pages.

faqs.q: Can I flatten a page that is badly curled?
faqs.a: Only gentle curves. The tool uses manual bend controls, not automatic dewarping, so heavy curls near the spine may not straighten fully.

faqs.q: Can I use this on a photo of a single loose page?
faqs.a: Yes. Any page photo with a gentle curve can be adjusted, not just book pages.

answer: Upload a page photo, choose Flatten curved page, and adjust the top and bottom bend controls. Preview the result, apply the correction, and export it. Scanner.cam's page flattener runs entirely in your browser: upload a photo of a curved book or notebook page, adjust the manual top and bottom bend controls, preview the correction, then apply and export. No signup, no upload. It handles gentle curves — it is not an automatic dewarping tool, and heavily curled pages near the spine may not straighten fully.

sections.heading: Straighten a gently curved page
paragraphs: Photograph a book or notebook as evenly as possible, keeping the entire page in frame. Select the page, open Flatten curved page, and adjust the two bend controls while watching the preview.
Apply the correction when the lines look more even. Use Undo to return to the prior page if the correction makes the scan worse.

sections.heading: What curve correction can and cannot do
paragraphs: The controls manually adjust vertical sampling between the top and bottom edges. They can help with gentle bowing, but they are not automatic three-dimensional reconstruction.
Deep folds, missing text, glare, or heavy shadows cannot be recovered reliably. Reposition the page, improve lighting, or take a new photo if the preview is unclear.
